consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS console, confirm you are signed in as the training IAM user, not root.

instructions.text: In the AWS console, confirm you are signed in as the training IAM user, not root.

consoleSteps.title: Configure default and aliased AWS dynamic credentials plus a sensitive variable
consoleSteps.instruction: Open HCP Terraform > fa-providers-terraform-providers-sensitive > Variables.

instructions.text: Open HCP Terraform > fa-providers-terraform-providers-sensitive > Variables.
Add Environment variable TFC_AWS_PROVIDER_AUTH with value true. Leave Sensitive off.
Add Environment variable TFC_AWS_PROVIDER_AUTH_LONDON with value true. Leave Sensitive off. LONDON is the tag for the aliased provider credential configuration.
Add Environment variable TFC_DEFAULT_AWS_RUN_ROLE_ARN with the ARN of fa-providers-terraform-run-role. Leave Sensitive off; an IAM role ARN is not a secret.
Add Environment variable TF_VAR_training_secret with value training-secret-not-real and turn Sensitive ON before saving.
Add Terraform variable aws_region with value eu-west-2, or rely on the default in variables.tf. Do not create AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY variables in HCP Terraform.
After saving TF_VAR_training_secret, confirm HCP no longer displays its value.
Understand the design: the default and LONDON configurations each request their own workload identity token, while the default role ARN supplies the same lab role to both.

tasks.goal: Create the complete HCP Terraform configuration with AWS, an AWS alias, Random, a child module and sensitive/ephemeral demonstrations.

consoleSteps.title: Build the multi-provider Terraform configuration
consoleSteps.instruction: Create C:\terraform-labs\fa-providers-terraform\hcp-main and a child folder modules\alias-demo.

instructions.text: Create C:\terraform-labs\fa-providers-terraform\hcp-main and a child folder modules\alias-demo.
Create versions.tf, variables.tf, providers.tf, main.tf, outputs.tf, .gitignore, modules\alias-demo\versions.tf and modules\alias-demo\main.tf.
Paste the supplied blocks into the matching files exactly.
Notice required_providers declares two provider TYPES: hashicorp/aws and hashicorp/random.

Notice there are two CONFIGURATIONS of the AWS provider: the default and aws.london. Both target eu-west-2 so this lab remains in the requested Region; the alias demonstrates configuration selection rather than cross-Region deployment.
Notice HCP Terraform supplies the tfc_aws_dynamic_credentials object at run time. The default provider uses .default.shared_config_file and aws.london uses aliases["LONDON"].shared_config_file.
Notice the child module declares configuration_aliases = [aws.london], and the root module passes aws.london explicitly.
Notice random_password.persisted_demo is a normal managed logical resource, while ephemeral.random_password.ephemeral_demo is intentionally not persisted in state.
Notice .gitignore excludes local state and tfvars but DOES NOT exclude .terraform.lock.hcl; the lock file should normally be committed to version control.

consoleSteps.instruction: Provider requirement: required_providers tells Terraform the provider source and acceptable versions.

instructions.text: Provider requirement: required_providers tells Terraform the provider source and acceptable versions.
Provider installation: terraform init installs/selects providers and writes concrete selections/checksums to .terraform.lock.hcl.
Provider block: configures a provider client, such as region or authentication-related settings.
Multiple provider types: this lab used AWS, Random and Vault.
Provider aliases: aws.london is a second configuration of the AWS provider. A resource/module must explicitly select/receive it; declaring an alias alone changes nothing.
Modules: provider configurations are defined in the root; child modules declare requirements and configuration_aliases, then the root can pass providers explicitly.

Authentication: local shared profile used long-lived bootstrap credentials; HCP remote runs used OIDC dynamic short-lived role credentials; Vault provider used a token from an environment variable instead of hard-coding it.
Sensitive: sensitive=true redacts normal display but values can still exist in state.
Ephemeral: values/resources marked/defined as ephemeral are omitted from persistent plan/state artifacts and may be used only in allowed ephemeral contexts.
Write-only: provider-defined write-only resource arguments accept values during an operation without persisting those argument values.
Vault: centralizes secrets and can issue dynamic secrets/credentials, but Terraform configurations using Vault must still protect state and avoid unnecessary secret persistence.

instructions.text: Confirm Task 19 destroy and AWS parameter verification are complete before deleting HCP state/workspace.
In HCP Terraform delete workspace fa-providers-terraform-providers-sensitive. Do not force-delete a workspace that still reports managed resources.
Delete project fa-providers-terraform-project after it is empty.
Delete the dedicated HCP organization whose name begins fa-providers-terraform- and ends with your recorded AWS account ID, but only if it was created solely for this Follow Along.

In the local Vault demo terminal, delete the fake secret if the dev server is still running, then stop the dev server with Ctrl+C. Because dev mode is memory-only, stopping the server removes its in-memory data.
In AWS IAM delete inline policy fa-providers-terraform-run-policy from role fa-providers-terraform-run-role, then delete the role.
Delete the app.terraform.io OIDC provider only if this Follow Along created it and no other workspace depends on it.

Sign in as root only to remove the temporary training IAM user's access key, delete user fa-providers-terraform-admin and delete customer policy fa-providers-terraform-admin-policy. Then sign out of root.
Remove only the [fa-providers-terraform-admin] sections from your local AWS credentials/config files or use aws configure commands to clear that named profile. Do not delete unrelated profiles.
Clear the current shell environment variables TF_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION, TF_WORKSPACE, VAULT_ADDR and VAULT_TOKEN.
Delete C:\terraform-labs\fa-providers-terraform last, after every cloud/HCP/authentication verification is complete.
Read and affirm the programme cleanup acknowledgement in the cleanup section.
